title: Epochal traffic braid and telemetry backstop for stream-preserving active-active failover
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Problem: For hosted API active-active deployments we need a deterministic, observable protocol to move traffic between regions without breaking long-lived streaming sessions or violating SLOs. Existing blunt cutovers cause client-visible stream resets, KV-cache divergence, or sudden latency/cost regressions.

This ticket introduces an "epochal traffic braid": an overlap-based, telemetry-gated traffic shift that moves small fractions of traffic per epoch while preserving streaming continuity, synchronizing ephemeral session state (KV prefixes and in-flight token cursors), and engaging progressive circuit breakers and load-shedding to protect SLO headroom. The mechanism must integrate with current gateway routing, runtime KV snapshot API, and streaming proxies.

Goals:
- Gracefully shift traffic between regions in active-active mode with per-epoch, observable progress.
- Preserve in-flight streaming sessions (HTTP chunked & WebSocket) wherever possible.
- Avoid cascading SLO failures by enforcing telemetry backstops and adaptive circuit-breakers.
- Provide clear rollback and audit traces for postmortems and customer support.
acceptance_criteria: Traffic can be shifted between two regions in <24 epochs (default epoch=10s) with per-epoch success metrics and no >2% increase in tail p95 latency for non-stream requests.
Active streaming sessions that are eligible for handoff complete or resume without visible token loss in >=95% of handoff attempts during a controlled canary shift (1000 sessions).
When telemetry backstop triggers (sustained headroom drop), the shift pauses within one epoch and automatically rolls back the last two epochs within 2x epoch duration.
Circuit-breaker policies engage progressively by epoch and are instrumented with per-epoch counts; errors/latency above configured thresholds cause immediate halt of further epochs.
Runbook documented and tested in staging; engineers can trigger a manual abort and force rollback with a single command that is audited in the routing history.
End-to-end integration tests exercising streaming handoffs, KV-sync, and rollback pass in CI with simulated packet loss and increased latency scenarios.
design_decisions: Use an epoch-based window (configurable, default 10s) rather than single-shot drains to reduce probability of large-scale streaming disruptions.
Implement ephemeral sticky proxies: gateways annotate requests with epoch id and handoff marker so downstream runtime can decide whether to continue the local KV path or stitch from a snapshot.
KV snapshot API: runtime exposes a lightweight snapshot token for prefix ranges; snapshots are taken asynchronously and propagated to target region prior to epoch shifts.

Telemetry backstop: gating is based on service-level headroom (P99 CPU load, queue depth, and observed p99 latency) aggregated per-region and per-model. A composite score below threshold pauses the braid.
Circuit breakers are per-route and per-epoch: initial epochs use conservative limits and widen if health signals remain stable for two consecutive epochs.
Load-shedding prefers failing fast (short-circuit responses) for non-critical routes and preconfigured API keys; streaming sessions get prioritized for graceful handoff where possible.
implementation_notes: Gateway changes: add epoch controller that coordinates per-route fractional weights and broadcasts epoch id to edges.
Runtime changes: implement snapshot and apply endpoints, idempotent apply semantics, and ephemeral token stitching for streaming cursors.
Proxy changes: streaming proxy must support token-preserve header and a short-lived handshake to transfer active stream ownership without TCP-level disconnect where feasible.

Create a new 'braid' orchestration service (stateless) that reads telemetry, computes epoch weights, and writes routing directives to the control plane; start with single-region pair implementation and extend.
Add safety toggles: max-epoch-progress-per-minute, epoch-timeout, and immediate-emergency-abort flag.
Performance-sensitive paths will fallback to byte-efficient snapshot formats; snapshot frequency is adaptive based on session churn.
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (dev): library-level mocks + unit tests for epoch controller and snapshot stubs (2w).
Phase 1 (staging): end-to-end with synthetic clients running 10k streaming sessions; validate handoff success >95% under normal conditions and >80% under induced packet loss (3w).
Phase 2 (canary): enable braid for 5% of production traffic for a low-risk region pair; telemetry backstop must be active and gate any progress; monitor for 72h (1w).
Phase 3 (gradual): increase to 25% then 100% across pairs after two successful canaries and postmortem reviews.
Phase 4 (global): enable configuration UI in Console for operators to start/stop braids and inspect per-epoch metrics (post rollout).
telemetry_and_alerting: Per-epoch metrics: shifted_fraction, handoff_success_rate_streams, handoff_fail_reasons (kv-missing, token-mismatch, proxy-timeout), epoch_duration_ms.
Composite health score per-region used by backstop: p99_latency_delta, sustained_cpu_headroom_pct, ready_worker_count_ratio. Alert if composite < 0.7 for >2 epochs.
SLO guardrails: create alerts when p95/p99 exceeds configured targets during an active braid and automatically pause progress on threshold breach.
Tracing: add epic-level trace id for each braid so we can correlate client session id -> epoch events -> runtime snapshot ids in traces.
Dashboards: braid overview, per-route epoch timeline, streaming handoff heatmap, rollback events and audit trail.
testing_plan: Unit tests for epoch arithmetic, backoff logic, and circuit-breaker state transitions.
Integration tests: simulated dual-region with induced latency/jitter and per-epoch verification of KV snapshot application.
Chaos tests in staging: kill workers mid-epoch, drop packets, and throttle disks to observe braid resilience and rollback behavior.
Load test: 50k concurrent streaming sessions with 10% churn; measure handoff success and end-to-end latency impact.
Manual runbook drills with SRE and on-call: trigger a failing braid and execute rollback in under 5 minutes.
rollback_plan: Automatic pause: telemetry backstop pauses progress and triggers automated rollback of last 2 epochs when composite health < threshold.
Manual abort: operator CLI 'braid abort --id <id>' stops new epoch issuance and triggers immediate reweight to previous steady state; operation is audited.
Fallback behavior: if stream handoff fails, affected sessions are pinned to origin region until TTL or client reconnect; ensure clear customer-visible error codes to aid client retry logic.
Post-rollback diagnostics: collect epoch traces, runtime snapshot diffs, and gateway routing logs into a single archive for postmortem.
open_questions: What minimum set of KV prefixes must be snapshotted to guarantee correctness for popular models? (ask model-infra team)
Can we avoid any TCP disconnects for WebSocket handoffs in current proxy design, or do we need light-weight in-proxy proxy-protocol?
Default epoch length tradeoffs: 5s vs 10s vs 30s — need perf runs to choose the default for global regions.
How to present braid state in Console for non-engineer operators (visual vs JSON directives)?
Should we make per-route braid defaults opt-in or opt-out for new customers?
